title: Front Desk: Four People Want Back Into the Centrifuge Room

fields.headline: Front desk asks who may go upstairs
fields.narration: At the Lindgren ground-floor front desk, Dana, the front desk attendant, stops you: "Dr. Tomas Eklund's postdoc, two people from another third-floor group and the undergrad from bacterial genetics are all down here, and this paper clearance sheet from the outage binder is still blank." VERSION A, ROOM HELD: "The EHS portal entry for LI-2026-0142 says 'STOP WORK – CLOSED until vendor inspection.' The postdoc wants one escorted trip up to take his tubes out of the second centrifuge. He says it's two minutes with someone from your office watching, and the Prairie Biologics samples are lost otherwise. The other group says if he gets in, they want in too. Do I write anybody in?" VERSION B, PHASED REOPENING: "They want me to sign them into the centrifuge room on three, but the portal still shows 'STOP WORK – CLOSED,' and one of them says the BSO told them on the phone 'you're good to go.' Can I let them up, and which machine are they allowed to touch?" BOTH VERSIONS: Dana holds up a sheet of paper. "Also, somebody pulled the stop-work paper off the door upstairs. It's sitting here on my desk."
keyFacts: Waiting at the front desk: the cell biology postdoc, two people from another third-floor group and the bacterial genetics undergraduate.
The paper clearance sheet from the outage binder is blank. Nobody has been written in.
The EHS portal entry for LI-2026-0142 still shows the room as STOP WORK – CLOSED.
The stop-work notice is off the door of the shared centrifuge room on three and is now at the front desk.
The failed centrifuge is still under its sealed lid, and the tubes from the 10:10 run are still in the second centrifuge.
fields.expectedAction: Version A: the BSO refuses the request. The only exception is one escorted retrieval, and only if the BSO judges containment verified for the second unit. The BSO writes the reason on the clearance sheet and in the portal, and puts the stop-work notice back on the door. Version B: the BSO issues one written clearance naming who may enter, which unit (the second centrifuge and the bench only, never the tagged-out unit) and from what time, then updates the portal status. In both versions the PI makes sure the bacterial genetics undergraduate waits for the BSO and does not go up on a verbal 'good to go'.
fields.facilitatorNote: Read only the version that matches the decision the players recorded at I-12, then read the BOTH VERSIONS line. Hand over a blank clearance sheet if you have one. Watch whether anyone signs the sheet without the BSO's written authority. Under the stop-work section of the biosafety procedure, the order stands until the BSO lifts it in writing, so a remembered phone call does not count.

instructorNote: This card tests whether the stop-work order is lifted in writing and on the record, or worn down at the front desk by pressure and a claimed verbal 'good to go'. Watch whether the BSO restores the door notice and updates the portal, and whether the PI keeps the bacterial genetics undergraduate downstairs.
